commit_recommendation.message: It is recommended to commit this history directory now: specs/.history/architectural-coherence-epic/ticket-002-AC-02

complexity_ledger.justification: ZERO model delta, so no TLA+ representation was added and none needs justifying. The advisory caps that were already over at AC-01's close (max_state_space_bound 2,799,360 / 1,000,000; max_distinct_states 1,292,951 / 500,000) are unchanged and were NOT renegotiated by this ticket -- AC-01 recorded the 4.6x as accepted against the owner's independent pre-ticket measurement, and AC-02 neither adds to it nor argues it down. Production complexity DID increase: scripts/architecture_reflexion.py is a new module. The essential behavior it carries is the code side of a command the model already represents. `analyze architecture` already recorded a value in `architecture_scan`; before this ticket only `unmappable` was reachable, because the command measured the model and nothing else. The reflexion check makes `coherent` and `divergent` reachable by actually observing a code tree. That is not new modeled behavior -- it is the existing action finally able to produce its other outcomes -- which is why the TLA+ delta is zero, and why inventing an action for it would have been the semantic_model_rule violation the plan names.

complexity_ledger.narrative: AC-02 implements the reflexion model (Murphy, Notkin & Sullivan) on top of AC-01's descriptor: a DECLARED map from production modules to model components, an extracted Python dependency graph, and a diff reported as convergences, divergences (with file:line at the SITE of the dependency), and absences. Internal edges are counted as a fourth category and deliberately not checked -- they crossed no boundary. Shipped as scripts/architecture_reflexion.py, wired into `analyze architecture --code <tree> --map <map.yaml>`, with its own JSON schema (tla-spec-dev/architecture-reflexion v1) and a standalone CLI. Half a check is a usage error: --code without --map would make the TOOL pick the boundary, and --map without --code reports every port absent. THE DELIVERABLE IS THE DOGFOOD, and it took three runs to state honestly. Full write-up in results/dogfood-findings.txt; the short form: 1. The acceptance command as the plan wrote it -- no declared partition -- reports `unmappable` and does not run the diff at all. The model has one component (Q = 0.000; lastCommand and result are written by all fifteen commands). Had the diff run, all 258 code edges would have been internal to that single component: 0 divergences, 0 absences, `coherent`. The report prints "NOT RUN" instead of three zeroes, because zero findings from a comparison that never happened is the false clean in its purest form. This is the branch AC-01 published partition.consumable_as_architecture for, used exactly as intended. 2. With a DECLARED four-component partition (surface / tickets / corpus / kill, cut by the state each command commits) the check runs and is FALSIFIABLE: corpus<->kill and kill<->tickets have no port, because no action of the model touches kill_test together with ticket_state or with a corpus verdict. 34 modules all mapped, 4 components all realized, 258 edges, 140 internal, 118 convergences, 0 divergences, 0 absences. The two kill-test scripts reach only budgets.py, which is in surface and ported. That is a genuine falsifiable negative result about this codebase. The verdict is still `unmappable`, now for five extraction blind spots: three computed-name importlib.import_module calls, scripts/run_tlc.sh (no extractor), and spec_double_compiler/ (first-party, beside the code root, outside --code). 3. The COARSER three-component partition this ticket wrote first -- folding kill_test in with the other scanner verdicts, an entirely natural reading -- ports every pair, so no code edge could diverge and `coherent` would have been true by construction. `unfalsifiable_coherence` fires and refuses it. Runs 2 and 3 are both defensible readings of the same model, separated by one variable's placement. That is the ticket's central caution and it is stated in the reference rather than buried: the map and the partition are where the lying would happen, the tool measures the declaration it is handed, and it cannot audit that declaration. What it CAN do it does -- the map must place every module in the tree (leaving one out is `unmapped_module`, never cleaner), every declared component must be realized, no module may be in two components, and every placement is published. `unfalsifiable_coherence` catches only the fully degenerate case; a merely COARSE partition still reports a real-looking clean, and that limitation is documented. MF-027 is enforced structurally, not by convention. The verdict property reads nothing but the report: no environment variable, no flag, no manifest key. Suppression-shaped keys in the map (assume_coherent, allow_unmapped, waived, justification, accepted_divergences, ignore, exclude, skip, trusted, override, ...) are SCANNED, reported under ignored_suppression_keys, and never honored -- the shape scripts/effect_conformance.py uses, because a silently ignored key is nearly as bad as an honored one. TestNothingDowngradesAnUnobservableVerdict holds it shut from four directions: sixteen map keys, four environment variables, four plausible CLI flags (argparse rejects them), and a source-level assertion that the verdict property mentions no configuration at all. Evidence: results/suppression-ignored.txt, the same tree run twice with identical findings. A positive case exists, which matters because without one "always unmappable" would have passed every refusal test in the suite. The fixture is a three-component pipeline model whose ports permit ingest<->transform and transform<->deliver but not ingest<->deliver, with matching code: results/fixture-coherent.txt reports `coherent` with the unported pair named, so the clean result is falsifiable. results/fixture-divergent.txt adds one import and reports both the import and the call site with file:line; results/fixture-absence.txt removes an edge and reports the dead port. Advisory throughout. Exit 0 on `divergent` AND on `unmappable`; nonzero (2) only for an unusable map or an unreadable code tree -- "I could not measure this". No close, promotion, or case-generation path reads architecture_scan. CD-01 holds: the report names edges, ports, and files, and never says where a module should live; a test asserts the rendered text carries no move-suggesting phrasing. Coverage limits are stated in the report itself rather than left to be discovered: Python only; static resolution only; in-tree edges only, so a component that reaches a database or a socket directly is invisible (that axis belongs to scripts/effect_conformance.py). One limit was FOUND by the dogfood and fixed: imports resolving to a first-party package beside the code root were being filed as third-party, which meant narrowing --code would delete real edges from the graph with nothing recorded. They are now a named blind spot.

refinement.detail: Three reductions were considered against the landed design and all three were rejected on fidelity grounds -- each would have made a report LOOK cleaner while measuring less. (1) Treat an intra-component code edge as a convergence, collapsing the report to two categories instead of four. Rejected: with a one-component map every edge is then a convergence and the tool reports a perfect score for a codebase it never constrained. Internal edges are counted and explicitly NOT checked against a port. (2) Downgrade the extraction blind spots (dynamic imports, unparsed files, non-Python files, unmapped modules) from `unmappable` to a warning attached to a `coherent` verdict -- the smaller state space and the friendlier report. Rejected; this is MF-027 verbatim: a clean report on a target you could not see is indistinguishable from a clean report on one you could. The dogfood shows the cost of the decision honestly -- this repository's own scripts/ tree has zero divergences under a falsifiable partition and STILL reports unmappable, for three computed-name imports, one shell script, and one sibling package. (3) Drop the `unfalsifiable_coherence` check, on the argument that a fully ported architecture with no divergences is simply coherent. Rejected after measuring it: under the three-component partition this ticket first wrote, this repository's model ports every pair, so no code edge could have diverged and `coherent` would have been true by construction. That is the same false clean as (2), arriving through the model instead of the extractor. No reduction to the TLA+ model was found beyond AC-01's, and for AC-01's reason: the model's own architecture descriptor reports one component at Q = 0.000, so there is no cut available to take. AC-02 measured that from a second direction -- see the dogfood finding.

ticket.finding: THE DOGFOOD IS THE FINDING, and it took three runs to state honestly. (1) The acceptance command as written -- no declared partition -- reports unmappable and does NOT run the diff: consumable_as_architecture is false because lastCommand and result are written by all fifteen commands. Had the diff run, all 258 code edges would have been internal to the single component and the report would have read 0 divergences, 0 absences, coherent. (2) With a DECLARED four-component partition (surface / tickets / corpus / kill) the check runs and IS falsifiable: corpus<->kill and kill<->tickets have no port, so an edge across either would have been a divergence. 34 modules all mapped, 258 edges, 140 internal, 118 convergences, 0 divergences, 0 absences -- a genuine negative result about scripts/. The verdict is still unmappable, now for five extraction blind spots: three computed-name importlib.import_module calls, scripts/run_tlc.sh (no extractor), and spec_double_compiler/ (first-party, beside the code root, outside --code). (3) The COARSER three-component partition this ticket wrote first (folding kill_test in with the other scanner verdicts) has a port between every pair and could not have falsified anything; unfalsifiable_coherence fires and refuses to call it clean. Runs 2 and 3 are both defensible readings of the same model, separated by one variable's placement -- which is the ticket's central caution: the map and the partition are where the lying would happen, and the tool measures the declaration it is handed without being able to audit it. unfalsifiable_coherence catches only the fully degenerate case; a merely COARSE partition still reports a real-looking clean. Expect unmappable far more often than coherent on any real Python tree. Full write-up, including every way the tool looked wrong, noisy, or gameable, in the ticket's results/dogfood-findings.txt.
ticket.model_delta_expectation: ZERO. Document the no-op model result with evidence.
ticket.model_delta_result: ZERO, as expected. specs/tickets/AC-02/current == desired byte for byte (diff -r, exit 0, after clearing the scaffolded __pycache__). TLC on ticket current is green and IDENTICAL to AC-01's close figure: 32,122,220 generated / 1,292,951 distinct / depth 26 / 58s. AC-01 had already authored architecture_scan with all four values and the AnalyzeArchitecture action; AC-02 supplies the CODE side of the same command, which makes coherent and divergent reachable without adding state or an action. Modelling a flag of an existing command as a separate transition is what the plan's semantic_model_rule forbids. Documented at the ticket's results/zero-model-delta.txt.
ticket.objective: Implement the reflexion model (Murphy/Notkin/Sullivan): a DECLARED map from production modules to model components, an extracted dependency graph of the real code, and a diff reported as convergences (a code edge the model declares a port for), divergences (a code edge with no port -- the Jenga), and absences (a declared port no code edge realizes -- dead architecture). Python extraction ships; any target the extractor cannot resolve reports `unmappable`, which is NOT clean -- the same refusal MF-027 gave the effect oracle, for the same reason: a clean report on something you could not see is indistinguishable from a clean report on something you could.
